name: Nguyen Anh
period: late 18th century (1777-1785 for this series; born 1762)
dynasty: Nguyễn lords (chúa Nguyễn); later founded the Nguyễn dynasty
role: Surviving prince of the Nguyễn lords who repeatedly fled the Tây Sơn, regrouped in the Mekong Delta and islands, and in 1802 became Emperor Gia Long
known_facts: Born in 1762, son of Nguyễn Phúc Luân, grandson of lord Nguyễn Phúc Khoát
1777: the Tây Sơn campaign in Gia Định ended with Tân Chính Vương Nguyễn Phúc Dương and Định Vương Nguyễn Phúc Thuần killed; Nguyễn Ánh, about 15, escaped
Late 1777: reappeared at Long Xuyên, moved to Sa Đéc with former generals such as Đỗ Thanh Nhơn, and raided Long Hồ
1778: Nguyễn forces retook part of Gia Định and Nguyễn Ánh was raised to supreme command
1782-1785: after defeats by the Tây Sơn he fled repeatedly — Ba Giồng, Phú Quốc, other islands — and sought help from Siam
1802: proclaimed Emperor Gia Long, founding the Nguyễn dynasty
interpretation: Late-18th-century southern Vietnamese noble youth on the run, plain period clothing, no crown or 19th-century imperial robe; appearance comes from the user reference.
unknowns: No verified contemporary portrait from 1777-1785 survives
The day-by-day route of the 1777 escape is not recorded
